long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Leningrad, Igor Sechin studied French and Portuguese at Leningrad State University and worked as an interpreter in Mozambique and Angola. He later joined St Petersburg's city administration, then moved through senior roles in Russia's presidential administration. From 2008 to 2012 he served as deputy prime minister, overseeing energy policy, before becoming president of Rosneft in 2012.

Sechin now serves as Rosneft's chief executive, management-board chairman and deputy board chairman. His wealth relationship is managerial: Rosneft discloses a personal holding of 0.1273 percent, while a federally owned vehicle remains the company's largest named shareholder. Public reporting has also documented substantial executive compensation. Those facts support an energy-sector, self-made executive profile, but they do not make Rosneft's wider state-company assets his private property.

uncertainties: The exact Forbes profile is verified, but it does not publish a net-worth estimate or a source-of-wealth field. Wealth classifications therefore rely on Rosneft disclosures and reputable reporting rather than treating Forbes profile existence as proof of a quantified fortune.

The Self-made classification describes the best-documented origin of Sechin's identifiable personal wealth: executive compensation and an acquired minority Rosneft holding. Public evidence does not establish his complete private balance sheet, so the classification is high rather than very-high confidence.

Rosneft is a state-controlled company. Its corporate value, revenues and wider assets were not counted as Sechin's private wealth; his wealth relationship is classified as Operator based on his management role and small disclosed personal stake.

Spanish authorities and El Pais attributed the 135-metre Crescent to Sechin, while Reuters reported that ownership was still under investigation when the yacht was detained. The relationship was used as supporting identity context but omitted from the biographies because public beneficial ownership was not conclusively established.

No second nationality was evidenced. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or dedicated personal website met the identity-verification threshold; a LinkedIn namesake in Virginia was rejected, and a prominent X account using Sechin's name has been reported as parody.
Blank suffix and secondary-residence fields were treated as optional, while death, internal-notes and unknown-name fields were treated as inapplicable while alive or system-controlled.
The replacement biographies deliberately focus on documented career and wealth relationships and omit unrequested allegations, political characterisations, sanctions context and nicknames.
